tavily_citations.title: SymPy Series Expansion Documentation
tavily_citations.content: When expanding expressions using .series(), the Order term O(x**n) tracks asymptotic behavior. If n is odd and highest non-zero power is even, order term retains n.

tavily_citations.title: Calculus and Power Series Algorithms
tavily_citations.content: In truncating alternating Taylor series, terms whose coefficient equals zero still evaluate to an order bound of the next non-vanishing degree.

ultra_diagnosis:
Root cause: In sympy/core/expr.py line 348, the series truncation cuts off at the degree of the last non-zero term instead of preserving the requested degree `n`. When expanding `cos(x)` at degree 4, the x**3 term is zero, causing premature truncation.
Fix: Ensure Order(x**n) uses the explicit parameter `n` rather than the highest discovered non-zero monomial.

@@ -348,3 +348,3 @@ def series(self, x=None, x0=0, n=6, dir='+'):
